anya (acme-mlx): Hi team — we're getting intermittent 500s when requesting cryptographic signatures for model keys. Started ~2026-03-16T22:14Z. Org: acme-mlx, key_id: key-79f2. Error samples attached in ticket. Can someone triage? :warning:
marco (support): Sorry — can you paste 1-2 request_ids and the exact timestamps? Are you on Redwood Private with CloudHSM or using hosted KMS? Any recent key rotations or config changes?
anya (acme-mlx): We're on Redwood Private (VPC) with AWS CloudHSM in us-west-2. We rotated the HSM cluster to 3 devices two days ago. Sample request ids: r-01f2a3, r-01f2a7, r-01f2b0 (timestamps 2026-03-16T22:14:03Z, 22:14:07Z, 22:15:41Z). Errors look like timeouts from the HSM client.
marco (support): Got it — pinging infra + security. @sam (security) @lee (eng-infra)
sam (security): Noted. Quick checklist: 1) Keys in CloudHSM are non-exportable — private key never leaves HSM. 2) CloudHSM has finite concurrency for cryptographic ops; if the app spikes it can queue and hit client-side timeouts. Please provide audit log slices and any HSM client logs.
lee (eng-infra): Seen this before when the client library opens too many short-lived sessions. Can you check our HSM client metrics on the host (session_count, open_handles, queue_len)? Also share p50/p95/p99 latency for sign ops from your side.
marco (support): Anya — can you run this two commands and paste output?
marco (support): ```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_TOKEN" "https://api.redwood.example/v1/audit?org=acme-mlx&start=2026-03-16T22:00:00Z&end=2026-03-16T23:00:00Z"
```
marco (support): and on the private host: ```
sudo journalctl -u redwood-hsm-client -o short-iso | grep "HSM sign" | tail -n 100
```
anya (acme-mlx): Pasted audit output to the ticket (INC-2026-0316-42). Journalctl shows repeated "session timeout" and "client queued" messages around the timestamps.
oncall-bot: Incident INC-2026-0316-42 created (P2) — assigned to support oncall.
cloudhsm-status-bot: No provider-wide CloudHSM outage reported in us-west-2.
sam (security): Since provider shows no outage, likely a local client or capacity issue. Two immediate mitigations: 1) enable HSM client connection pooling and reuse sessions; 2) add a short-term fallback signing path for low-latency ops (software key wrapped by HSM) while we investigate. Note: fallback must be auditable and flagged in logs for compliance.
lee (eng-infra): Config recommendation (temporary): set REDWOOD_HSM_MAX_CONN=120 and REDWOOD_HSM_SESSION_TTL=300 to encourage pooling, and increase client-side timeout to 2s. Also patch the client to use async sign calls if not already. We'll push a config change to the private hosts if you authorize.
marco (support): Can we repro in our staging cluster? Lee, can you run a synthetic load: 50 concurrent sign requests to the same key to see queuing behavior? Here's a curl xargs example to reproduce:```
seq 1 50 | xargs -n1 -P50 -I{} curl -s -X POST "https://private-host.internal/v1/sign?key=key-79f2" -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TEST' -d '{"digest":"abcd"}'
```
lee (eng-infra): On it — running now. If we see p99 > 300ms and high queue_len we'll capture thread stacks.
anya (acme-mlx): We're open to the fallback approach for now, as long as audit trails show who triggered it and keys are still under HSM custody for primary ops. Is there a documented process for wrapping a software key with CloudHSM?
sam (security): Yes — we can do a wrapped-key approach: create an ephemeral software signing key, encrypt (wrap) it with the HSM master key so only HSM can unwrap for verification during key import. This preserves custody semantics for the master key but does expose ephemeral key material on the host. Must record the wrap operation in audit logs and restrict host access. I'll prepare a short compliance checklist.
marco (support): Next operational steps: 1) customer approves temporary config change -> we apply pooling/timeouts; 2) eng runs repro and captures p99 + queue_len; 3) security drafts wrapped-key checklist and acceptance criteria; 4) we open an escalation with AWS CloudHSM (we'll include packet captures and client logs).
lee (eng-infra): Repro finished in staging: observed p50 ~25ms, p95 ~180ms, p99 ~610ms under 50 concurrent sign ops; queue_len spiked and client reported "no available sessions". Attaching flamegraph to ticket.
marco (support): Thanks. Anya — can we schedule a screen-share tomorrow 10:30 PT to apply config changes and walk through fallback checklist?
anya (acme-mlx): Yes please. Also asking about on-prem HSM support — we may move to a hardware appliance in our colo. What models are supported?
sam (security): We support Thales Luna and Gemalto/Thales Luna HSMs and can integrate Thales nShield in private deployments. Requirements: FIPS 140-2/3 mode, remote attestation enabled, and HSM must support key wrapping and import tokens. We'll send the compatibility matrix.
marco (support): Final notes: created subtask INC-2026-0316-42-01 for config change, assigned to lee; INC-2026-0316-42-02 for security checklist assigned to sam; INC-2026-0316-42-03 for provider escalation (support lead). We'll update the customer after the call. :white_check_mark:
